title: fragmentation-shepherd-evictor-and-spillpack-coalescer-for-kv-cache
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Production KV cache fragmentation and micro-spill I/O were increasing eviction churn and end-to-end tail latency for small continuous-batch workloads. This PR introduces a fragmentation-aware eviction policy (the 'fragmentation shepherd') that prioritizes compaction-friendly candidates, coordinates asynchronous compaction, and groups spill I/O into contiguous 'spillpacks' to reduce small-file write amplification.

What this PR does: implements a new eviction scorer that combines occupancy variance, slab fragmentation entropy, and recent-access hotness to pick candidates that can be coalesced with neighbors rather than leaving many tiny fragments. Adds an async compaction scheduler that uses continuous-batching telemetry (batch arrival patterns and idle windows) to pick low-impact times to compact hot regions. Adds a spillpack writer that bundles multiple evicted pages from the same tenant/shard into a single contiguous spill object and emits a lightweight manifest for rehydration. The evictor exposes tunables: fragment_threshold, spillpack_max_pages, quarantine_backoff_ms, compaction_budget_ms.

Design notes: the fragmentation score is normalized per-slab to avoid cross-slab bias. We integrated a kernel-heatmap hint into routing: when compaction is selected, the request can be routed to nodes whose selected kernels are optimized for memmove/compaction (e.g., vectorized memcopy kernels on upcoming backends) to reduce compaction CPU cost. The async compactor uses a two-phase op: lightweight metadata merge first (fast) then an optional rewrite if fragmentation exceeds rewrite_threshold.

Compatibility and safety: default behavior is opt-in via config flag kv.fragmentation_shepherd.enabled=false. When enabled, the system starts in conservative mode (low compaction_budget_ms, small spillpack sizes) and can be ramped. Mechanisms added: soft-quarantine prevents immediate re-insertion of recently-evicted items to avoid thrash; a health gate checks spillback I/O queue depth and defers compaction if IO pressure is high.

Testing and benchmarks: unit tests for the scorer and spillpack manifest, integration test against synthetic fragmentation workloads, and mem-leak/regression CI added. Benchmarks run on a 4-GPU staging cluster with a tenant mix (50% small requests driven by continuous batching traces). Results: eviction count reduced by 29% on average, small-spill-file count reduced by 84%, overall KV-tail p99 eviction latency improved 18ms, P95 end-to-end request latency unchanged within noise (+/-1ms). Token cost per request reduced by ~6% due to fewer repeated fetches after compaction.

Rollout plan: feature flag -> Canary on dedicated capacity only -> 2-week observation period with metric dashboards (spillpack_size distribution, compaction CPU ms, quarantine drops) -> enable for broader fleet.

Checklist: [x] implementation, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] benchmarks, [x] rollout plan, [x] docs in runtime/kv/README.md (short note and config explanation).

Related work: follows ENG-1791 (fragmentation telemetry), complements ENG-1820 (spillback backpressure shaping).

Notes: This PR focuses on the eviction/compaction control plane and spillpack format; it avoids changing on-disk swap formats for blocks to keep upgrades safe. Future follow-ups will add telemetry-driven auto-tuning for fragment_threshold and an experimental proactive compactor that rewrites cold slabs in maintenance windows.
